name: alice and an ice-lite server

input.local:
a=candidate:1 1 udp 2130706431 192.168.1.42 50004 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 192.0.2.10 54321 typ srflx raddr 192.168.1.42 rport 50004
a=candidate:3 1 udp 16777215 198.51.100.50 49152 typ relay raddr 192.0.2.10 rport 54321

why: The post's call: three local candidates against the server's one host. Two checks, host first and the relay last, through TURN. Pair priorities priced by hand with G the controlling agent's: host-host 2^32*2130706431 + 2*2130706431, relay-host 2^32*16777215 + 2*2130706431.

expect.caption: Computed check order, highest priority first. Local side controls

name: alice and an ice-lite server, the pairs

input.local:
a=candidate:1 1 udp 2130706431 192.168.1.42 50004 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 192.0.2.10 54321 typ srflx raddr 192.168.1.42 rport 50004
a=candidate:3 1 udp 16777215 198.51.100.50 49152 typ relay raddr 192.0.2.10 rport 54321

why: The srflx pair, sent from its base 192.168.1.42:50004, would send the same check as #1, the host pair, so it is pruned. Its own price, 2^32*1694498815 + 2*2130706431, would put it second.

expect.caption: Pruned: this pair sends the same check, from the same place to the same place, as one above

a=candidate:1 1 udp 2130706431 192.168.1.42 50004 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 192.0.2.10 54321 typ srflx raddr 192.168.1.42 rport 50004

a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 198.51.100.77 40100 typ srflx raddr 10.0.0.8 rport 61000
a=candidate:3 1 udp 16777215 198.51.100.51 49200 typ relay raddr 198.51.100.77 rport 40100

why: The same nine pairs with G and D swapped: equal-priority pairs now break the tie the other way, by the (G>D?1:0) term. The candidate priorities themselves do not change, only which side is G.

fields.label: Controlling
fields.note: Its candidate priorities are G in the pair formula, the other side's D.

fields.label: Pair priority
fields.value: 2^32 x min(G, D) + 2 x max(G, D) + (G > D ? 1 : 0)

name: mdns and ipv6

input.local:
a=candidate:1 1 udp 2122260223 7f3c1b2e-4d5a-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e.local 50004 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 2122262783 2001:db8::42 50006 typ host
a=candidate:3 1 udp 1686052607 192.0.2.10 54321 typ srflx raddr 0.0.0.0 rport 0

why: A browser's mDNS name pairs with the IPv4 server; the IPv6 host does not, and the srflx with a hidden raddr cannot be traced to its base, so it is kept. No relay on either side, but the server's host address is public, so that is a note rather than a warning.

expect.caption: What to look at, most serious first

columns.label: What it means and what to do

rows: Neither side has a relayed candidate, but the remote side has a public host address.
That usually connects. Only a network that blocks UDP stops it; a TURN server over TCP or TLS on port 443 is the fallback.
1 local reflexive candidate does not say which host address it was learned from.
Browsers hide it as raddr 0.0.0.0. Its pairs are kept here; if the host it came from is listed, the browser prunes them.
1 candidate has nothing to pair with: local host 2001:db8::42:50006.
A pair needs the same component, transport and address family on both sides. An IPv6 candidate needs an IPv6 one on the other side.

name: no relay anywhere is a warning

input.remote:
a=candidate:1 1 udp 2130706431 10.0.0.8 61000 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 198.51.100.77 40100 typ srflx raddr 10.0.0.8 rport 61000

why: Two browsers behind NATs and no TURN server: if either NAT maps per destination every check fails, so it is a warning, listed straight after the check order.

expect.caption: What to look at, most serious first

columns.label: What it means and what to do

rows: Neither side has a relayed candidate, so there is no fallback through a server.
If a firewall blocks UDP, or both NATs give a new port per destination, every check fails and the call never connects. Add a TURN server to iceServers.
